slides.say: Given: x is equal to fourteen a plus six, a is a positive integer, and x is divisible by ten. Which of the following could be the value of a?

So x is fourteen a plus six, and that whole result must be divisible by ten. A number divides by ten when its last digit is zero. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, working out which last digit a needs, and then testing the choices.

[short pause] Let's start with the last digit of x. Remember, a number divides by ten when its last digit is zero. x is fourteen a plus six, and we need that result to end in zero. What last digit could fourteen a have, so that adding six gives a last digit of zero? It must end in four, because four plus six is ten. So fourteen a ends in four.

Now let's find the last digit of a. To find a product's last digit, we only need the last digit of each number we multiply. Fourteen ends in four. So four times the last digit of a has to end in four. Four times one is four, and four times six is twenty-four. No other digit works. So a must end in one or six.
Now check the numbers in the choices. We need a number ending in one or six. Only three hundred forty-six fits: it ends in six. So choice number four is our answer.
at: choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to test the choices, with last digits only. Each choice gives a possible a. We need fourteen a plus six to end in zero. Let's test three hundred forty-three. Its last digit is three. Four times three is twelve, so fourteen a would end in two. Two plus six is eight, so x would end in eight, not zero. That choice is out.

Now test three hundred forty-four. Four times four is sixteen, so fourteen a would end in six. Six plus six is twelve, so x ends in two, not zero. Out. Now test three hundred forty-five. Four times five is twenty, so fourteen a would end in zero. Zero plus six is six, so x ends in six, not zero. That choice is out too.
at: so fourteen a would end in zero

slides.say: Three choices are out, leaving three hundred forty-six. So choice number four is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
